# bsllmner-viewer

> Ontology-mapped annotations of public BioSamples, linked to their SRA experiments and BioProjects. bsllmner-mk2 extracted cell lines, cell types, tissues, diseases, drugs, genetic perturbations, and ChIP antigens from the free-text BioSample attributes with an LLM, and mapped each value to an ontology term. This site queries, counts, and exports those annotations.

Use the JSON API rather than the pages. Every page of this site shows the result of one API query, and the API returns the same result.

## API

- [Swagger UI](/api): every endpoint with its parameters, and requests that you can try
- [OpenAPI document](/api/openapi.json): the contract of the API
- [API specification](https://github.com/dbcls/bsllmner-viewer/blob/main/docs/api.md): the conventions, the condition language, and how counts are computed
- [Data model](https://github.com/dbcls/bsllmner-viewer/blob/main/docs/data-model.md): records, annotation statuses, and counting units

## Conditions

Every query takes one condition string, `q`. The language is the Lucene subset of the DDBJ Search API: `field:value`, `field:"phrase"`, `field:[a TO b]`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses. Text without a field is a keyword that matches the searchable text of a BioSample, such as `hypoxia organoid` or `"breast cancer"`.

- `disease:"MONDO:0007254"` matches breast cancer and every descendant term.
- `cell_line:"CVCL:0030" AND library_strategy:ATAC-seq` matches HeLa ATAC-seq experiments.
- `organism_id:9606 AND date_published:[2015-01-01 TO 2020-12-31]` matches human BioSamples published from 2015 to 2020.
- `disease_status:unmapped` matches BioSamples whose disease value has no ontology term.

`GET /api/dataset` lists the fields of the language. `GET /api/terms?query=<text>` finds the term IDs to use in a condition.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/entries/biosample?q=`: the matching BioSamples, one page at a time (`page`, `perPage`)
- `GET /api/entries/biosample/{accession}`: one BioSample with its attributes, annotations, and the evidence of each annotation
- `GET /api/distribution?field=&q=`: counts per term or value of one field
- `GET /api/crosstab?row=&col=&q=`: counts per pair of two fields, with expected counts that reveal gaps
- `GET /api/trend?q=`: counts per year of BioSample publication
- `GET /api/projects?q=`: BioProjects of the matching BioSamples
- `GET /api/export/accessions/{type}?q=`: every matching accession of `biosample`, `sra-experiment`, `sra-run`, or `bioproject`, as one `#` header line and then one accession per line

## Notes

- Counts are counts of records. A record is a BioSample with one of its SRA experiments. The `unit` parameter counts distinct BioSamples, experiments, or BioProjects.
- Annotations come from an LLM and can be wrong. Each annotation has a status that tells how its term was chosen, or why it has none.
- Every response has `datasetVersion`. Keep it with results that you record, because counts change with each build of the dataset.
- Errors are RFC 7807 problem documents. A query parameter that the endpoint does not declare gives 422, so check the spelling (`q` is the condition, `query` is the search text of `/api/terms`). A condition or a field that the dataset rejects gives 400, and the `type` ends with the name of the rule. Status 503 means that the API is busy or that a query took too long: wait for the `Retry-After` seconds, or narrow the condition. More than 100 requests in progress from one address give 429 with `Retry-After`: send fewer requests at a time.
- A condition has at most 4096 characters, 16 keywords, and 64 keyword words. A request names at most 100 elements of a dimension, and the `limit` of `/api/crosstab` is at most 100.
